description: Costs 1 credit. Loads a page and returns its main content as clean Markdown, with the title, description, Open Graph fields, word count, an estimated token count, and a content-quality flag. This is the right tool for reading a page — it is the cheapest option and returns text rather than an image. Use domscout_capture_screenshot only when you actually need to SEE the page. By default the served HTML is read first and the browser runs only when that comes back thin, so static pages (documentation, blogs, news, changelogs) answer quickly and client-rendered ones still get JavaScript. meta.renderJs says which one answered. Set fast:true to never start a browser, or fast:false to always start one. Same price either way. Without DOMSCOUT_API_KEY it runs on a keyless demo limited to a few calls an hour.

delay.description: Extra milliseconds to wait after load.

fast.description: Leave unset to let the service choose. true: read only the served HTML, never a browser; a client-rendered page may come back empty, and it cannot be combined with waitForSelector, delay or lazyScroll, which need a live page. false: always run the browser.

lazyScroll.description: Scroll the page first to trigger lazy-loaded content. Adds 1 credit. Needs a browser, so it cannot be combined with fast:true.

url.description: The page to load. Must be http(s) and publicly reachable. Credentials in the URL (https://user:pass@host) are rejected; these tools capture as an anonymous visitor, so use the REST API directly if the page needs authentication.

waitForSelector.description: Wait for this CSS selector to appear before capturing.

name: domscout_extract_markdown
title: Read a page as clean Markdown
